seed: Blending is the row under Opacity that says HOW a layer mixes with what is under it, rather than always painting straight over. This walk opens a real settings-pane screenshot, draws one solid box over a row of it, then opens the Blending list and takes the box through all five choices in turn, photographing each over the same backdrop so they can be read side by side. It finishes by undoing back to Normal. Canvas coordinates are window points measured down from the top-left of the editor view.

steps.note: the capture as it arrived, nothing touched
one solid box drawn over a row of the screenshot. It covers what is under it completely, which is what every layer has always done
THE TEST for the words: the list is open and every choice carries a plain sentence beside its name, so a person who has never used Photoshop can pick the right one without trying all five
THE TEST: the box burns its colour into the row underneath and the words show through it, the way a highlighter pen works. One step to undo
the same box lightening instead, as though a light were shone on the region
keeps whichever is darker, so the box shows only where the screenshot is lighter than it
and the other way round: only where the screenshot is darker than the box
THE TEST for undo: each choice was one step, so four presses walk back through them to the solid box it started as
a highlight mark, the one layer with no Blending row: mixing is what makes it a highlighter, so the panel says so rather than offering five choices that would all do nothing
